Let <MATH_0001> be a morphism of algebraic stacks
representable by algebraic spaces. Then the following are equivalent
<STRUCT_0001>
<STRUCT_0002> <MATH_0002> is quasi-separated,
<STRUCT_0003> <MATH_0003> is quasi-compact, or
<STRUCT_0004> <MATH_0004> is of finite type.
<STRUCT_0005>

The statements
``<MATH_0001> is quasi-separated'',
``<MATH_0002> is quasi-compact'', and
``<MATH_0003> is of finite type''
refer to the notions defined in
Properties of Stacks,
Section <REF_0001>.
Note that (2) and (3) are equivalent in view of the fact that
<MATH_0004> is locally of finite type by
Lemma <REF_0002>
(and
Algebraic Stacks, Lemma
<REF_0003>).
Choose a scheme <MATH_0005> and a surjective smooth morphism <MATH_0006>.
Set <MATH_0007> which is an algebraic
space by assumption, and the morphism <MATH_0008> is surjective
and smooth. By
Categories, Lemma <REF_0004>
and
Properties of Stacks,
Lemma <REF_0005>
we see that we have: <MATH_0009> is quasi-compact if and only if
<MATH_0010> is quasi-compact.
If (1) holds, then <MATH_0011> is quasi-separated and we see that
<MATH_0012> is quasi-compact, i.e., (2) holds.
Assume (2) holds. Let <MATH_0013> be a scheme, and <MATH_0014>
a morphism. Set <MATH_0015>. To prove
(1) we have to show that the morphism of algebraic spaces <MATH_0016>
is quasi-separated. Using
Categories, Lemma <REF_0006>
once more we see that <MATH_0017> is the base change of
<MATH_0018>. Hence our assumption (2) implies that <MATH_0019>
is quasi-compact, hence <MATH_0020> is quasi-separated as desired.
